title: U.S. House · Maryland's 8th District
area: Most of Montgomery County, including Rockville, Bethesda and Silver Spring.

context.text: Incumbent Jamie Raskin defeated J.D. Kumar, Stephen Leon and Boris Velasquez in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Cheryl Riley defeated Anita Cox, Donald Lech and Michael Yadeta in the Republican primary. Nancy Wallace advanced on the Green Party line; no individual Ballotpedia profile or campaign materials for her were found.

summary.text: Jamie Raskin is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 8th Congressional District. A former constitutional law professor and Maryland state senator, he serves as the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C.; earned his bachelor's degree and law degree from Harvard University.
Worked as a law professor at American University's law school and as an assistant attorney general in Massachusetts.
Served in the Maryland Senate before his election to Congress in 2016.

priorities.text: Addressing climate change, including past support for a market-based carbon pricing approach paired with renewable energy investment.
Reducing gun violence, citing his work passing a comprehensive Maryland gun safety law in 2013.

positions.summary: Per his 2016 campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia, worked with then-state Senator Brian Frosh to pass what the page describes as one of the most comprehensive state gun safety laws in the nation in 2013.
Per his 2016 campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia, says he will work to dramatically reduce greenhouse gas emissions and invest in clean energy such as solar and wind power.
Joined the Maryland delegation in a letter urging House Republican leaders to extend the ACA enhanced premium tax credits and warning of Medicaid losses under H.R. 1.
positions.quote: we urge leadership to act swiftly to extend the ePTCs

positions.summary: Said he voted against House Republicans' budget resolution to provide billions more in taxpayer funding for ICE and CBP.
positions.quote: House Republicans’ latest scheme to funnel billions of taxpayer funding toward Donald Trump and Stephen Miller’s reign of ICE lawlessness

record.text: Serves as ranking member of the House Committee on Judiciary for the 2025-2026 term.
Served on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, chairing its Civil Rights and Civil Liberties Subcommittee, during the 2021-2022 term.

summary.text: Cheryl Riley is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 8th Congressional District, a public relations executive making her second run for the seat.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C., and grew up in Montgomery County, Maryland; took classes at Montgomery College and the University of Maryland, College Park.
Works as a public relations executive.

priorities.text: Public safety, saying she would support giving police officers more latitude.
Reducing the tax burden on residents.
Creating affordable housing options for all residents.

summary.text: Nancy Wallace is the Green Party nominee for Maryland's 8th Congressional District.

researchNotes: No individual Ballotpedia profile, campaign website, or Candidate Connection survey was found for Green Party nominee Nancy Wallace; only her name appears on the state candidate list.
